column2: 中古英语 reprochen ← 古法语 reprochier（责怪）
column3: to express disapproval of someone, or such blame itself
column5: She reproached him for arriving late.|His look carried silent reproach.
column6: holding a fault up before someone – 把过失举到人面前
column7: 责备：因过失而当面说不是|指责：明确指出对方错处

column2: 中古英语 reptil ← 古法语 reptile ← 晚期拉丁语 rēptile，为 reptilis（爬行的）的中性形 ← 拉丁语 rēpere（爬）
column3: a cold-blooded animal with scales, such as a snake or lizard
column5: This reptile basks on warm rocks.|Snakes and lizards are reptiles.
column6: a scaled creature that creeps along – 覆鳞而贴地行进的生物

column2: 中古英语 rescouen ← 古法语 rescoure ← 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ excutere（摇出、驱出），后者由 ex（出）＋ quatere（摇）构成
column3: to save someone from danger, or such an act
column5: Lifeboats rescued four sailors that night.|The rescue took nearly six hours.
column6: shaking someone free of danger – 把人从险境里抖脱出来
column7: 营救：出动人力把人救出|解救：使摆脱困境或束缚

column2: 近代早期 ← 法语 rechercher（细查）← 古法语 recerchier（寻找），相当于 re-（再）＋ search
column3: careful study to discover new facts
column5: Her research changed the whole field.|They research rare diseases here.
column6: searching again and again into something – 反复往里搜寻
column7: 研究：系统探求新知|调查：为弄清事实而查问

column2: 借自盎格鲁诺曼语 resemblance ← 古法语 ressemblance，由 resemble ＋ -ance 构成
column3: the state of looking like something else
column5: The resemblance between them is striking.|I see little resemblance here.
column6: the degree of seeming alike – 看上去相像的程度
column7: 相似：整体上看着像|相似之处：具体某一处相像

column2: 中古英语 resemblen ← 古法语 ressembler，由 re-（加强）＋ sembler（看似）构成
column3: to look or be like someone or something
column5: She resembles her grandmother closely.|The copy resembles the original exactly.
column6: seeming the same as another – 显得与另一个一样
column7: 像：外形上跟某人某物相近|类似于：性质或情形与之相近

column2: 借自法语 réservoir（贮存处），源自 réserver（保留）
column3: a large lake built to store water
column5: The reservoir supplies the whole city.|Rain refilled the reservoir by May.
column6: a place where something is kept in store – 把东西存起来的处所
column7: 水库：拦蓄水的人工湖|蓄积：储存起来的大量某物

column2: 中古英语 resorten ← 古法语 resortir（退回、求助），由 sortir（出去）反构而成
column3: a place people go to for holidays, or to turn to something for help
column5: The seaside resort fills up every August.|They resorted to legal action.
column6: falling back on something – 退回来倚靠某处
column7: 度假地：供人休假游玩的地方|求助于：别无办法时转而依靠

column2: 借自中古法语 ressource ← 古法语 resource（泉源），源自 resourdre ← 拉丁语 resurgere（再涌起）
column3: a supply of something useful that can be drawn on
column5: Water is a scarce resource here.|The company lacks the resources to expand.
column6: a spring that rises again when drawn on – 取用后仍会再涌起的泉源
column7: 资源：可供取用的自然或人力储备|财力：可动用的钱物

column2: 古英语 ræst ← 原始西日耳曼语 *rastu ← 原始日耳曼语 *rastō，更早词源不明
column3: a period of not working, or the part that is left
column5: She took a short rest under the tree.|The rest of the group went ahead.
column6: a pause in effort, and what stays over – 停下的那一段，以及留下的那一份
column7: 休息：停下活动以恢复|其余：剩下的那一部分

column2: 借自法语 restaurant，为 restaurer（恢复）的现在分词 ← 拉丁语 restaurāre（修复）；得名于最初店家所售的「恢复元气」的汤
column3: a place where meals are cooked and served to customers
column5: They opened a small restaurant downtown.|The restaurant closes at eleven.
column6: a place serving food that restores you – 供应能补回元气的饭食之处

column2: 中古法语 retirer（拉回）← 古法语 retirer，由 re-（回）＋ tirer（拉）构成
column3: to stop working at the end of a career, or to withdraw
column5: He retired after forty years there.|She retired to her room early.
column6: drawing oneself back out of the field – 把自己从场上拉回去
column7: 退休：到年限后不再工作|退出：从某处或某活动中撤离

column2: 中古英语 retreve ← 古法语 retrover（重新找到）的词干，由 re-（再）＋ trover（找到）构成
column3: to bring something back, or to find stored information
column5: The dog retrieved the ball at once.|Users can retrieve old files easily.
column6: finding again and bringing back – 重新找到并带回来
column7: 取回：把东西拿回原处或手中|检索：从存储中查出所需信息

column2: 中古英语 returnen ← 古法语 retourner ← 中世纪拉丁语 retornāre（转回），由 re-（回）＋ tornāre（转）构成
column3: to come or go back, or to give something back
column5: They returned home before the storm.|Please return the book by Friday.
column6: turning back the way one came – 沿原路转回去
column7: 返回：回到原来的地方|归还：把借来的东西交回

column2: 中古英语 revelen ← 古法语 reveler ← 拉丁语 revēlāre（揭去覆盖），由 re-（去掉）＋ vēlāre（覆盖，出 vēlum 幕布）构成
column3: to make something known or visible
column5: The report revealed serious safety faults.|Fog lifted and revealed the coast.
column6: taking the veil off something – 把幕布从上面揭掉
column7: 揭示：把隐藏的情况公开出来|显露：使原本看不见的呈现出来

column2: 中古英语 revelacioun ← 古法语 revelacion ← 拉丁语 revēlātiō（揭露），源自 revēlāre（揭去覆盖）
column3: a surprising fact made known, or the act of making it known
column5: The letter contained a real revelation.|His account was a revelation to us.
column6: what comes to light once the cover is off – 幕布揭开后显出的事
column7: 启示：忽然明白过来的道理|揭露：把隐情公开这件事

column2: 借自中古法语 revenge，源自 revenger ← 古法语 revengier，与 vengier 同支 ← 拉丁语 vindicāre（索偿、报复）
column3: harm done to someone in return for harm they caused
column5: He took revenge for the insult.|Revenge solved nothing in the end.
column6: claiming back the harm one suffered – 把所受的损害索讨回来
column7: 报复：以害还害|复仇：为旧怨而施加报复

column2: 中古英语 revewe ← 古法语 reveue，为 reveoir（再看）的过去分词阴性形 ← 拉丁语 revidēre，由 re-（再）＋ vidēre（看）构成
column3: a written judgment of a work, or to look over something again
column5: The book got excellent reviews everywhere.|Please review these figures before Monday.
column6: looking at something over again – 把东西再看一遍
column7: 评论：审阅后写出的评价|复查：重新查看一遍

column2: 中古英语 reviven ← 古法语 revivre ← 拉丁语 revīvere（再活），由 re-（再）＋ vīvere（活）构成
column3: to come back to life or strength, or to bring something back
column5: Warm tea revived him within minutes.|The company revived an old design.
column6: coming to life once more – 重新活起来
column7: 复苏：从衰弱或停顿中恢复|使复兴：让已衰落的重新兴起

column2: 借自法语 révolter ← 意大利语 rivoltare（翻转），与拉丁语 revolvere（滚回）同支
column3: to rise up against authority, or such an uprising
column5: The soldiers revolted against their officers.|The revolt spread through the province.
column6: turning right over against a ruler – 对当权者整个翻过来
column7: 起义：武装反抗当权者|反抗：拒不服从并对抗

column2: 1557 年起见于记载 ← 拉丁语 rhythmus ← 希腊语 rhythmos（有度的流动），源自 rhein（流）
column3: a regular repeated pattern of sound or movement
column5: The drummer kept a steady rhythm.|Her breathing settled into a slow rhythm.
column6: a measured flow that returns evenly – 均匀回还的流动
column7: 节奏：声音或动作的规律起伏|韵律：诗文或乐句中的声调格式

column2: 中古英语 riban ← 古法语 riban／ruban，更早词源不明；后一半或与 band 同源
column3: a long narrow strip of cloth used for tying or decoration
column5: She tied the box with red ribbon.|A ribbon marked her place in the book.
column6: a long narrow strip for binding – 用来系束的细长条
column7: 丝带：细长的织物条|缎带：面上带光泽的丝带

column2: 古英语 rǣdels（谜、揣度）← 原始西日耳曼语 *rādislī，由 rede（劝告、揣度）＋ -le 构成
column3: a question worded so that the answer is hard to guess
column5: He asked the children an old riddle.|Her silence remained a riddle.
column6: a question set to be guessed at – 出来让人去猜的问题
column7: 谜语：故意绕着说的猜题|难题：一时想不通的问题

column2: 借自拉丁语 rīdiculus（可笑的），源自 rīdēre（笑）
column3: so silly that it deserves laughter
column5: The excuse sounded completely ridiculous.|He wore a ridiculous hat that day.
column6: inviting laughter by being absurd – 荒谬得引人发笑
column7: 荒唐的：不合情理到离谱|可笑的：让人忍不住要笑

column2: 中古英语 rigorous ← 中古法语与盎格鲁诺曼语 rigoreus ← 晚期拉丁语 rigōrōsus（僵硬、不通融）
column3: very careful and following strict rules
column5: The tests follow rigorous safety standards.|She kept rigorous notes throughout.
column6: held stiff to the rule with no give – 硬照规矩来、不留余地
column7: 严格的：一丝不放松地照标准来|严密的：环节紧扣没有漏洞

column2: 拉丁语 rītuālis，由 rītus（礼）＋ -ālis 构成
column3: a set of actions always done the same way, or relating to such actions
column5: The morning ritual never changes here.|They performed the ritual in silence.
column6: a fixed order of acts repeated as a rite – 按礼制固定下来的一套动作
column7: 仪式：按固定次序进行的一套举动|仪式性的：属于这类举动的

column2: 借自拉丁语 rōbustus（坚实如橡木），源自 rōbur（橡木、力）
column3: strong and not easily damaged
column5: The bridge has a robust steel frame.|She stayed robust well into old age.
column6: as tough as oak – 像橡木那样结实
column7: 强健的：身体或体质结实|坚固的：结构耐得住冲击

column2: 中古英语 romauns ← 古法语 romanz（法兰西白话，与拉丁语相对）← 中世纪拉丁语 rōmānicē（用罗马话），源自 rōmānus（罗马的）
column3: a love affair, or a story of adventure and love
column5: Their romance began one summer evening.|He writes historical romances now.
column6: a tale told in the common tongue – 用白话讲出的故事
column7: 恋情：两人之间的爱情|传奇故事：讲爱情与冒险的叙事作品

column2: 由 romant ＋ -ic 构成，或借自晚期拉丁语 romanticus（具传奇作品气质的）
column3: connected with love, or suited to expressing love
column5: They planned a romantic dinner together.|The film tells a romantic story.
column6: in the manner of a love tale – 带着爱情故事那种情味的
column7: 浪漫的：富于情致而不拘实际|爱情的：与男女情爱有关的

column2: 由 round ＋ about 复合而成，20 世纪初起见于记载
column3: a circular road junction where traffic goes one way around
column5: Take the second exit at the roundabout.|He gave a roundabout explanation.
column6: a way that goes around instead of straight – 绕着走而不直穿的路径
column7: 环形交叉路：车辆绕中心岛依次驶出的路口|迂回的：不直截了当而绕着来的
